niche.habitat: 20–25 km redox layer; persistent volcanic plumes; high-altitude convective bands
niche.diet: Atmospheric H2S, SO2, CH4, and photochemical oxidants via epidermal symbionts
niche.active: Continuous drift; foraging bursts during storms and dusk

body: Wide, rigid sail membrane reinforced by silica spicules; dense iron-sulfur core; porous epidermis housing symbiont clusters; conductive spines along leading edges

chains.trait: Wide, silica-reinforced sail drifts on dense air
links: High gravity (1.36 g) demands maximum lift efficiency
Dense atmosphere (2.5 kg/m³) enables drag-based lift
Volcanic emissions supply abundant silica aerosols
Colony incorporates silica into membrane skeleton to catch wind and filter particles simultaneously

skill.effect: The creature effortlessly glides on rising winds and thick air currents.

chains.weakness: Grounded by still air; cannot climb without thermal or wind uplift.
observe: Membrane holds rigid convex shape against wind
No beating wings; drifts like a stone in water

journal.en: [Speculative] The reef swims the sky on a wing of ash, trading agility for endurance.

plausibility.summary: State explicitly: colony is neutrally buoyant or slightly positive in the redox layer via porous volume and metabolic gases; surface 2.5 kg/m³ matters for acoustic impedance and sub-cloud dynamics, while altitude holding is updraft- and storm-dependent (weakness already). Drop “drag-based lift” as a substitute for reduced gravity; use “convective loft + low bulk density.”
fixes: State explicitly: colony is neutrally buoyant or slightly positive in the redox layer via porous volume and metabolic gases; surface 2.5 kg/m³ matters for acoustic impedance and sub-cloud dynamics, while altitude holding is updraft- and storm-dependent (weakness already). analogues.organism: Portuguese man-o’-war float and sail; glass sponges (silica spicule skeleton); thistledown and spider ballooning for passive aerial transport.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Epidermal symbionts oxidize H2S into metabolic energy
links: Low O2 (6%) limits aerobic respiration efficiency
Redox layer provides high flux of H2S and SO2
Symbionts use H2S/O2 or H2S/oxidant couples for high-energy thioester chemistry
Colony integrates sulfide-scavenging bacteria into epidermal pores to feed directly from air

skill.effect: When near volcanic vents or storm runoff, the creature absorbs harsh gases to sustain itself and shares vitality with nearby allies.

chains.weakness: Starves rapidly if H2S/SO2 supply is blocked; symbionts die in clean air.
observe: Porous skin hisses faintly as gas exchanges
Bioluminescent glow pulses in symbiont clusters
Odor of rotten eggs near colony

journal.en: [Speculative] Its skin breathes fire without flame, turning poison into sustenance.

plausibility.summary: Tone down ally O₂ to a small halo or storm-time pulse unless symbionts are oxygenic; note symbiont failure below a redox flux threshold (already in weakness).
fixes: Tone down ally O₂ to a small halo or storm-time pulse unless symbionts are oxygenic; note symbiont failure below a redox flux threshold (already in weakness).

analogues.organism: Riftia pachyptila and other vestimentiferans with intracellular sulfide-oxidizing symbionts; Beggiatoa and Thiomicrospira colorless sulfur bacteria on H₂S gradients.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Sharp spines act as lightning rods and charge sensors
links: Frequent lightning (15 flashes/km²/yr) creates local electric fields
Fair-weather 150 V/m rises to 1–3 kV/m under cells
Colony evolves conductive spines to sense voltage gradients and ride updrafts
Spines also discharge stored charge to stun predators and attract prey to bio-lights

skill.effect: The creature crackles with stored electricity, drawing nearby foes inward and disrupting their strikes.

chains.weakness: Spines attract destructive lightning strikes; players can use grounded rods to redirect bolts.
observe: Sparks jump between spines during storms
Colony tilts toward storm centers and charge sources

journal.en: [Speculative] It wears the storm's anger as a crown, harvesting the sky's wrath.

plausibility.summary: Reframe Engage as orientation (tilt toward cells/updrafts), prey attraction via bioluminescence (F23), and painful corona/tactile zap at contact—not battlefield-wide air arcs. Keep “lightning rod” risk as primary hazard.
fixes: Reframe Engage as orientation (tilt toward cells/updrafts), prey attraction via bioluminescence (F23), and painful corona/tactile zap at contact—not battlefield-wide air arcs. Keep “lightning rod” risk as primary hazard.

chains.trait: Iron-rich core stores spores and provides ballast
links: High gravity pulls spores fast; ballast needed for controlled descent
Iron core provides mass for spore dispersal to ground
Iron and sulfides shield sensitive spores from high background radiation (0.01 mSv/h)
Colony releases spores in bursts when injured or at end of life cycle

skill.effect: The creature releases a heavy cloud of iron-rich spores that obscures vision and settles over the ground.

chains.weakness: Core damage is fatal; piercing attacks or sonic resonance can crack the core.
observe: Ash cloud bursts contain glowing metallic flecks

journal.en: [Speculative] A heart of stone beats in the cloud, anchoring the reef's future.

plausibility.summary: Specify core as compact spore cyst with magnetite–pyrite matrix, not bulk metallic heart; spore release on senescence/injury is plausible, “sonic crack core” is **highly speculative**—prefer thermal or desiccation cracking at dusk cooling tied to F3 weak seasons + altitude temperature swing.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria (intracellular magnetite chains); fungal and plant spores with mineral coats; submarine/ballast logic (dense payload, buoyant superstructure).

temperament: Passive drifter; lashes out when highly charged; vulnerable to acoustic shock and ground-level isolation
secrets: The iron core yields 'Magnetite-Chunks' when harvested; used to craft high-density ballast weights or magnetic resistors for player gear.
Symbionts can be extracted to create a temporary 'Sulfur-Resist' buff, but the extract degrades rapidly without continuous H2S supply.
moments: At dusk, the iron core thermally cracks as the temperature drops, releasing a reverse snowstorm of blue-green bioluminescent spores that drift through the ochre haze like falling stars, illuminating the reef's silhouette against the darkening sky.

journal.en: [Speculative] The reef does not grow on rock; it grows on the breath of the world, filtering the volcano's sigh.
A sky-fish with no fins, eating the storm's electricity and the air's sulfur.
